WHAT: Python script that compares native vs WhisnapKeyboard screenshots pixel-by-pixel

WHERE: Whisnap-IOS/tools/keyboard_diff.py (runner: tools/run-keyboard-comparison.sh)

HOW IT WORKS:
1. Takes two screenshots (native + whisnap), crops to keyboard region
2. Detects key contours via white threshold (cv2.findContours)
3. Samples key BACKGROUND at top-left corner (not center — avoids letter glyphs)
4. Measures glyph size by finding dark pixel bounding box within each key
5. Outputs HTML report with side-by-side + heatmap + per-key table

KEY METRICS REPORTED:
- Background color delta (RGB) — 0 delta means colors match
- Key dimensions (width x height in px and pt)
- Glyph bounding box in pt
- Overall pixel difference % (5x amplified heatmap)

GOTCHA: Dark mode detection uses threshold=60 (not 128) for contour finding. Emoji page uses different threshold because emoji cells aren't white rectangles. Overall pixel diff is ~17% mostly because of toolbar area (expected different).

RUN: `bash tools/run-keyboard-comparison.sh` — captures Maestro screenshots for all pages then runs diff
